clue.text: Rough sort of sports ground

definitions.meaning: approximate, as in a rough estimate or figure
an arena or stadium where baseball and other games are played

explanation.surface: Someone describes a rough-and-ready kind of playing field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' just joins the two senses: a rough figure is a 'ballpark' one.
explanation.definitionFit: An approximate estimate is called a ballpark figure, and a baseball stadium is a ballpark.

clue.text: Human beings are terribly despicable, but not Alec

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters of the word despicable are mangled into a new order
but not tells us some letters, those of the name Alec, are left out of the rearrangement

explanation.surface: A cynical remark that humanity is vile, with one man named Alec excepted.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of DESPICABLE, remove A, L, E and C, and rearrange the remaining D, S, P, I, B, E.
explanation.definitionFit: People walk on two legs, so humans are two-footed creatures of that kind.

clue.text: The fat on bears regularly viewed as a food store

parts.note: lard is pig fat used in cooking

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word bears

explanation.surface: Bears stockpiling blubber are seen as keeping a pantry.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of 'bears' give ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantry or cupboard where provisions are kept is a larder.

clue.text: Delight at being left in parking facility

indicators.note: in says the letter for left goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
facility can mean ease, as in doing something with facility

explanation.surface: Someone is delighted at being dropped off in a car park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parking facility' looks like one phrase (a car park) but splits into P and EASE; L goes in after the P.
explanation.definitionFit: To delight someone is to give them pleasure, a synonym used as a verb.

clue.text: Saucepan emptied into badly prepared fish

indicators.note: into tells us the kept letters are placed inside the rearranged ones
badly signals that the word prepared is rearranged, as if done wrong
emptied means removing the inside letters of the word Saucepan, keeping its first and last

explanation.surface: A cook tips a saucepan's contents over a poorly cooked fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emptied' keeps only the first and last letters of 'Saucepan'; 'badly' scrambles the other word, and 'into' slips the kept pair inside that anagram after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A red snapper is a reddish sea fish eaten widely, an example of the general term.

clue.text: The train stops here, old boy!

definitions.meaning: a shock-absorbing barrier at the end of a railway track
a mildly comic term for a fussy old man

explanation.surface: An announcement at a terminus that ends with a jovial 'old boy!'
explanation.definitionFit: A railway stop-block absorbs a train's impact, and 'old buffer' is British slang for a doddery elderly man.

clue.text: Bowling over? No!

parts.note: in cricket, bowling with the arm swung over the shoulder is the norm; the opposite style keeps the hand below the shoulder

explanation.surface: Someone denies being knocked flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowling over' suggests knocking someone down, but read it as a cricket bowling style: not overarm, so the other kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Delivering a ball with the hand below shoulder level is the opposite of the overarm action.

clue.text: What to eat during Lent?

parts.note: Lent is a season of fasting, so the food then would be the kind suited to a fast

explanation.surface: A question about the proper diet for the Christian season before Easter.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase normally means quick meals like burgers; here 'fast' is read as abstaining from food during Lent.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick takeaway meals go by this name, and the joke reads 'fast' as religious abstinence.

clue.text: Dora's failed attempt at MOT?

indicators.note: failed suggests the name Dora goes wrong and is jumbled

parts.note: the possessive adds no letters; the name Dora is the fodder
a test is a trial or attempt

explanation.surface: Dora has another go at her car's annual inspection and doesn't pass.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's compulsory annual roadworthiness check for vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: The British vehicle inspection is a trial of whether a car is fit to drive on public highways.

clue.text: Forecastsfinalbetweenbetween Barcelona and Liverpool, say

clue.text: City model does Salvation Army!

indicators.note: model as a verb means shape or remould, so the word does is reshaped

explanation.surface: A town's fashion model takes up work for the Salvation Army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' looks like a noun, but it is the anagram signal: DOES becomes ODES. ODESSA is a Ukrainian port on the Black Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major Black Sea port city in Ukraine.

clue.text: The salad cream is in the window table

definitions.meaning: a sauce such as vinaigrette or mayonnaise poured on salad
the word fits between 'window' and 'table' to make two familiar phrases

explanation.surface: A diner notes the salad cream is on the table by the window.
explanation.walkthrough: The second part is a fill-in: the word completes 'window ___' (shop display) and '___ table' (a bedroom table with a mirror).
explanation.definitionFit: Salad cream is a sauce for salad; window displays and bedroom mirror-tables both take this word.

clue.text: Paid athlete able to make money?

parts.note: a professional sportsperson is a pro
able in body means fit, capable

explanation.surface: A question whether a salaried sportsman can earn a living.
explanation.definitionFit: To gain financially, earning more than one spends, is what this verb means.

clue.text: Fiddle cost, or even get some insurance papers

indicators.note: fiddle means tamper with, so the letters of cost, or, even are shuffled

explanation.surface: Advice to fiddle the price or break even by obtaining insurance documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' looks like fraud, matching the insurance surface, but it signals rearranging COSTOREVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Temporary certificates issued by insurers before the full policy arrives are called this.

clue.text: Winning shout, and debts become hilarious

parts.note: a side that is winning is up, ahead in the score
a roar is a loud shout
IOUs are written promises to pay, so debts

explanation.surface: A victorious cry, and money owed turns into something very funny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winning shout' looks like a single cheer, but the two words give separate pieces; 'and' and 'become' just join the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wildly funny, causing loud laughter, is described this way.

clue.text: Rowing in the washhouse?

parts.note: rowing with oars is sculling, and the back kitchen where washing up is done might whimsically be where it happens

explanation.surface: A question about a quarrel breaking out in the laundry room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rowing' suggests arguing (rhymes with 'cow'), but read it as rowing a boat: sculling, hence the room name.
explanation.definitionFit: A back kitchen for washing dishes and laundry is this room, punningly linked to sculls.

clue.text: Fast food ban here? Absolutely not!

definitions.text: Fast food ban here? Absolutely not!

parts.words: Fast food ban here? Absolutely not!
parts.note: the place's name could be read as a prohibition on quick bites, yet it is just where they are sold

explanation.surface: Someone indignantly denies that takeaways are prohibited in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: The name reads like 'bar snacks' in the sense of banning them, but the place exists to sell them.
explanation.definitionFit: A counter or café selling light quick meals is called this; 'bar' can also mean prohibit.

clue.text: Greek bread -nice, but not one measly bit!

parts.note: pitta is a flat Greek bread

indicators.note: but not tells us to take the letter for one away from the word nice

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A diner says Greek flatbread is pleasant but none of it should be left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nice, but not one' leaves NCE once the I is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny, inadequate amount of money or anything is a measly sum.

clue.text: Thought the Tory left, perhaps, communist

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the Tory party
left is an example of a side, along with right
red is a common term for a communist

explanation.surface: A political musing about a Tory, maybe on the left, who is a communist.
explanation.walkthrough: The political words look like one picture, but each gives a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To have thought something through carefully is to have weighed it, a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Home is where it is hot!

definitions.text: Home is where it is hot!

parts.words: Home is where it is hot!
parts.note: plays on the saying about home and the heart, and on the warm spot at the centre of a house

explanation.surface: A homely saying twisted to praise the warmth of one's house.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying is 'home is where the heart is'; the fireplace is the hot centre of the home, and the word contains 'heart' plus H for hot.
explanation.definitionFit: The floor of a fireplace stands for domestic life and warmth, so it symbolises home.

clue.text: Soldiers hand out a nasty experience

parts.note: OR stands for Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers
to deal is to hand out, as cards

explanation.surface: Troops distributing something unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful or trying trial that one must endure is this kind of experience.

clue.text: Charlie fails and shuts down

parts.note: Charlie is the radio code word for the letter C
to lose is to fail, as in a contest

explanation.surface: A man named Charlie goes bust and his business ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' looks like a person but is the phonetic alphabet's C.
explanation.definitionFit: Ending operations or shutting up shop is what a business does when it ceases trading.

clue.text: Place delayed admitting commander

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: something delayed is late
OC is the military abbreviation for Officer Commanding

explanation.surface: A venue is held up by letting in an officer.
explanation.definitionFit: To find or position something is to locate it; place here is a verb.

clue.text: Changes relating to the whole?

indicators.note: changes means the letters of the word relating are altered in order

explanation.surface: A question about alterations that concern the entire thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relating to the whole' looks like the definition, but 'relating' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Integral means complete, entire, or essential to the overall thing.

clue.text: Being silly about second class going out

indicators.note: about means going round, so the rearranged letters surround the class letter
silly suggests the word Being is jumbled foolishly

parts.note: B denotes second class or grade

explanation.surface: Someone acting foolishly over a second-class seat on the way out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' makes EBING from BEING, and 'about' puts B inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide retreating is said to be falling back, as an ebb tide goes out.

clue.text: King surrounded by viewers with no clothes on!

indicators.note: surrounded by puts the letter for king inside the word for viewers

parts.note: starers are people who gaze, viewers
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch encircled by onlookers while naked, like the emperor in the fable.
explanation.walkthrough: STARKERS is British slang for stark naked.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for stark naked, wearing nothing at all.

clue.text: Northern city ball?

parts.note: a delivery in cricket shares its name with a native of a northern English city

explanation.surface: Asks about a dance held in a city in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket this is a ball pitched right at the batsman's feet; the name could also mean someone from YORK, the northern English city.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket delivery aimed at the batsman's toes, named, it is said, after the northern English city.

clue.text: Surfaces roads when parking stops

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as he left
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
halts means stops

explanation.surface: Roads are given a coating whenever parking is suspended.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay a tarry bitumen coating on highways is the verb sense used here.
